answer: The system resists clones by comparing how each identity writes. Every identity must hand-copy a fresh 14-line sonnet with a plume, in one sitting, once every 7 days, timed on camera down to each line. Software compares timing patterns across identities: two records that mirror each other, matching pauses on at least 12 of 14 lines within half a second, count as one operator and share one payment. One hand cannot produce two different stroke patterns in one sitting, so 50 clones need 50 separate sittings, and writing for two merges both records.
